label: Worsening (pandemic reversal)
rationale: Global HALE at birth fell from its 2019 peak of 63.5 years to 61.9 years in 2021, a 1.6-year drop that erased roughly a decade of gains. No official data exists beyond 2021, so the recovery trajectory is unknown; national life-expectancy proxies show only partial recovery.

label: Distant
rationale: Current 10-year solid tumor survival is roughly 50–60% overall, and metastatic cases cluster at 8–35% five-year survival, far from the 80% target. 2025 brought new approvals and the MSK MMRd immunotherapy-only trial (~80% response), but the target needs transformational advances in late-stage treatment.

label: Approaching
rationale: Only ~14% of US and ~6% of UK cancers are detected through screening, with effective screening for just 4–5 cancer types. 2025 brought strong momentum: the first FDA-cleared Alzheimer's blood tests and PATHFINDER 2 showing a 7× cancer-detection increase, with MCED tests approaching FDA PMA (expected H1 2026); cardiovascular and metabolic pre-symptomatic detection still lag.

label: Distant
rationale: Dementia prevalence after age 80 is ~17–24%, 4–5× the 5% target. Anti-amyloid therapies slow but do not stop decline, and 2025 saw failures of oral semaglutide and the anti-tau antibody posdinemab plus fatal ARIA-E safety warnings for Leqembi.

label: Approaching (but not achieved)
rationale: Best demonstrated human biological age reversals cluster around 2–4 years, far short of the 10-year threshold. The OpenAI/Retro >50× reprogramming-efficiency result and partial reprogramming moving toward human trials are promising.

label: Distant: no measured pre-symptomatic share for any NCD class; tools cleared, >50% not in sight
rationale: The ledger has no measurement, and so no trend, of the milestone's own quantity: the share of major NCD cases caught before symptoms. The verified FDA-cleared Alzheimer's blood tests (Lumipulse, Elecsys pTau181) are for patients with cognitive symptoms, not for pre-symptomatic screening. The multi-cancer results (PATHFINDER 2, Cancerguard) are legacy proponent reports with no population-scale uptake, and there are no cardiovascular or metabolic records. With no evidenced path to >50% across the four disease classes, the ETA exceeds 10 years (red).

basis.rule: Milestone red: no evidenced path. There is no measured value or trend of the milestone's quantity (share of major NCDs caught pre-symptomatic); tool clearances and a trial whose results are only expected (projection) cannot lift a status; ETA >10 years
basis.eta: >10 years (not estimable: no series of the pre-symptomatic detection share in the ledger)
basis.path: None evidenced at population scale. Cancer: MCED tests (Galleri PATHFINDER 2: >7x detection when added to USPSTF screening, 53.5% early-stage; Cancerguard launched), both legacy proponent reports; NHS-Galleri RCT results only expected (projection). Neurodegeneration: FDA-cleared blood tests for symptomatic evaluation. Cardiovascular/metabolic: no evidence records
blockers: Evidential: no population-level measurement of pre-symptomatic detection for any of the four disease classes
Technical/regulatory: no MCED test has regulatory approval or a mortality-benefit RCT result in the ledger; the cleared AD blood tests are indicated for symptomatic patients
basis.benchmark: >50% of major NCD cases (cancer, cardiovascular, metabolic, neurodegeneration) caught pre-symptomatic
basis.change_note: Rubric correction v1, no new evidence; yellow -> red. The previous assessment scored momentum, not the milestone's quantity: it relied on test clearances and a trial whose results were only expected ('FDA PMA expected H1 2026', NHS-Galleri results mid-2026). Projections and announcements never lift a status under STATUS.md. Its '~14% US / ~6% UK cancers detected through screening' level has no evidence record, it cited superseded records (Lumipulse, Elecsys), and its label 'Approaching' is not a v1 verdict and gave no level or benchmark.

label: Distant: US 5-yr survival 69% all cancers, metastatic 8-31% vs goal 80% of solid tumors at 10 yrs
rationale: The latest level in the ledger is 69% 5-year survival for all US cancers and 8-31% for stage IV disease (ACS/SEER 2025, legacy); 10-year survival is necessarily lower, far from 80% of solid tumors surviving 10 years. The ledger has no survival time series to extrapolate. The verified 2025 FDA approvals (Datroway, avutometinib+defactinib, imlunestrant, Pluvicto expansion) are incremental per-indication gains, and the NCI budget faces a proposed 37% cut. No evidenced path reaches the goal within 10 years (red, Distant).

basis.rule: Milestone red: ETA >10 years on the evidenced path. The level (5-yr survival 69% all cancers; metastatic 8-31%) is far below 80% at 10 years, and no evidenced path or survival trend closes the gap within 10 years
basis.eta: >10 years (no survival time series in the ledger to extrapolate; the gap from 69% at 5 yrs and 8-31% for metastatic disease to 80% at 10 yrs is not closed by per-indication approvals)
basis.path: Incremental per-indication therapies: 2025 FDA approvals (ADCs, targeted agents, radioligands, CAR-T) and immunotherapy-only responses in MMRd tumors (NEJM, legacy); none shifts all-solid-tumor 10-yr survival at scale
blockers: Technical: metastatic disease remains largely incurable (stage IV 5-yr survival 8-31%)
Funding/policy: FY2026 request proposes a 37.3% NCI budget cut
basis.benchmark: 80% of solid tumor cases reach 10-year survival
basis.change_note: Rubric correction v1, no new evidence; status stays red, but its grounds are corrected. The previous label 'Distant' gave no level or benchmark. Its '10-year solid tumor survival roughly 50-60%' has no evidence record, and it cited the superseded FDA-46-drugs record. It also cited an unverified funding-cut figure instead of the corrected 37.3% NCI request. Red now rests on the evidenced level and the lack of any path closing the gap within 10 years.

label: Distant: ~17-24% at 80+ vs <5% goal; incidence -20% over 2-3 decades, >100 yrs to goal
rationale: Dementia prevalence after 80 is about 24% at ages 80-89 (US ADAMS, legacy), and the NHS gives 1 in 6 over-80s for Alzheimer's alone, against a target below 5%. The only trend evidence is a ~20% fall in age-standardized incidence over 2-3 decades in high-income countries (Lancet Commission 2024, legacy), about 0.7-1.1%/yr relative; extrapolated, reaching 5% takes more than 100 years. Interventions help only at the margin: intensive BP control gave RR 0.85 (verified) and anti-amyloid drugs slow decline, while oral semaglutide failed Phase 3 (verified). The ETA is therefore well over 10 years (red, Distant).

basis.rule: Milestone red: ETA >10 years by trend extrapolation. A ~20% incidence decline per 2-3 decades (0.7-1.1%/yr relative) takes ln(17-24/5)/rate = ~110-210 years to reach <5%
basis.eta: >100 years on the evidenced incidence trend (110-210 years if prevalence tracks age-standardized incidence)
basis.path: Risk-factor reduction (cardiovascular health, education; intensive BP control RR 0.85) plus anti-amyloid drugs that slow decline (donanemab -27% progression risk at 3 yrs, legacy); no intervention prevents or reverses dementia at scale
blockers: Technical: disease-modifying therapies slow but do not stop decline; 2025 Phase 3 failures (oral semaglutide, posdinemab)
basis.change_note: Rubric correction v1, no new evidence; status stays red, but its grounds are corrected. The previous label 'Distant' gave no level or benchmark. Its rationale leaned on trial setbacks rather than a trend-extrapolated ETA, and it used a ~17% dementia figure from the NHS record that re-verification corrected (the NHS figure is 1 in 6 for Alzheimer's). It also cited superseded records (NHS prevalence, oral semaglutide). Red now rests on the evidenced incidence trend giving an ETA of >100 years.

label: Stalled: best human clock reversal ~2.5-3.2 yrs (2019-2025) vs >=10 yrs; no disease-incidence data
rationale: The best human biological-age reversals in the ledger are 2.5 years (TRIIM 2019), 3.23 years (Fitzgerald 2021) and 2.6 years (Buck TPE+IVIG 2025), all legacy, so the 2025 result shows no gain on 2019-21. None of these trials shows the reductions in age-related disease incidence that the milestone also requires. The larger 7.42-year figure is an in-vitro preprint (SB000), the OpenAI/Retro result measured reprogramming efficiency rather than organismal age, and human reprogramming trials are only planned or just dosed. With the milestone quantity stalled, the ETA exceeds 10 years (red).

basis.rule: Milestone red: stalled. The best demonstrated human biological-age reversal shows no progress between two windows (2019-21: 2.5-3.2 yrs; 2025: 2.6 yrs), and there is no evidence of reduced disease incidence; ETA >10 years
basis.eta: >10 years (no upward trend in demonstrated human reversal to extrapolate; the disease-incidence clause needs multi-year outcome trials that have not started)
basis.path: Candidates only: in-vitro/preclinical reprogramming (SB000 preprint, GPT-4b micro factor variants); first-in-human trials planned (Life Biosciences ER-100, an announcement) or just dosed (Retro RTR242, an autophagy drug); senolytics setback (UNITY liquidated)
blockers: Technical: no human intervention exceeds ~3 years of epigenetic-clock reversal; partial reprogramming is not yet in human efficacy trials
Evidential/definitional: 'validated' needs clock plus functional biomarkers plus reduced disease incidence; no outcome trial exists
basis.benchmark: >=10 years of biological-age reversal (epigenetic clocks + functional biomarkers) with reduced age-related disease incidence
basis.change_note: Rubric correction v1, no new evidence; yellow -> red. The previous assessment called the milestone 'Approaching' while its own figures showed best human reversals of 2-4 years, unchanged since 2019. It lifted the status on an in-vitro reprogramming-efficiency result and on trial plans and first dosing (announcements), which cannot lift a status. It also ignored the disease-incidence clause, and its label was not a v1 verdict and gave no level or benchmark.

label: Behind pace: 62.9y (2021); ex-COVID +0.10/yr 2017-19 vs +0.16/yr 2000-19 own trend (tier 3)
rationale: Median-country HALE at birth (WHO GHE, 185 countries) rose 64.1 -> 64.3 years over 2017-2019, a +0.10 yr/yr trend; the window mean of 64.20 is 0.44 years above the previous non-overlapping window 2012-2016 (63.76, slope +0.04 yr/yr), about 2.6 times the residual SD of the 2000-2019 fit, so the trend is clearly upward. That pace is below the tier-3 benchmark, the series' own 2000-2019 OLS trend of +0.156 yr/yr, so the status is yellow (Behind pace). The 2020-2021 COVID-19 fall to 63.4 and then 62.9 years spans under one 5-year window, has a named cause and an expected reversal (national life expectancy has largely recovered by 2022-2024 per ONS UK, US CDC and JAMA California), and no later GHE year has been published, so it is discounted as a transient; including it, the 2017-2021 slope is -0.32 yr/yr. The 2022 GHE observation will confirm or reverse the transient; if it does not show recovery, the status turns red.

label: Distant: US 5-yr survival 69%, stage IV 8-31% vs 80% at 10 yrs; ~1%/yr hazard gains, ETA ~2063
rationale: US 5-year relative survival for all cancers is 69% (ACS 2025) and stage IV 5-year survival is 8-31%. That implies ~62% 10-year survival against the 80% target, a 1.9x gap in the non-surviving fraction. Non-survival has historically fallen ~1.0-1.2%/yr. With modest acceleration (median 1.5%/yr) from ADCs, bispecifics, immunotherapy and early detection, plus the 10-year follow-up floor, the median ETA is ~2063 (80% range 2042 to after 2100). That is far beyond 10 years, so red (Distant).

basis.rule: Milestone red: median ETA 2063 > made_at + 10 yr (RUBRIC.md §4: Distant)

eta.method: trend (exponential hazard reduction of the 10-yr non-surviving fraction, US frontier proxy) + structural floor (10-yr follow-up), Monte Carlo; cross-checked against a reference class and the prev ETA
eta.calc: Gap: 10-yr survival ~62% (5-yr 69% x ~0.90 conditional 5->10; breast 10-yr 86%) vs 80% -> non-survival 38% -> 20% = 1.9x (0.93 halvings). Historical rate (ACS, background): 5-yr survival 49% (1975-77) -> 69% (2014-20) = ln(51/31)/41 = 1.21%/yr; 67% -> 69% (2008-14 -> 2014-20) = 1.04%/yr. Time = ln(1.9)/r: r 1.1% -> 58 yr -> cohort 2071, observed ~2078; r 1.5% -> 43 yr -> cohort 2056, observed ~2063; r 3% -> observed ~2041. MC (N=200k): r ~ lognormal(median 1.5%, p10 0.8%), S10 ~ U(0.58, 0.66) for 2013 cohorts, observation lag U(5, 9) yr -> p10 2042.4, p50 2062.5, P(by 2100) 0.90; the global reading is later -> p90 null. P(by Oct 2036) 0.03. AI driver (robots-software metr-50-horizon-by-release 0.05 -> 1044.78 min 2019-02 -> 2026-04, ~6-month doubling; 2025-01-01-ai-drugs-75-in-trials) shortens discovery but not trials or the 10-yr follow-up. Prev v1 ETA was '>10 years', a band.
eta.cruxes: Earlier: US cancer mortality decline accelerating to >3%/yr; NHS-Galleri/MCED mortality benefit and uptake; mRNA vaccine (mRNA-4157) OS benefit across tumour types; durable stage IV survival with ADC/bispecific regimens. Later: NCI cut enacted; flat 5-yr survival in the next ACS releases; screening lead-time artefacts. Gather: an all-site 10-yr relative survival series (SEER/CONCORD/CRUK).

basis.path: Incremental per-indication gains (2025: 46 novel FDA drugs, ADCs/bispecifics; Datroway, avutometinib+defactinib, imlunestrant, Pluvicto, tarlatamab), immunotherapy-only responses in MMRd tumours (~80%), mRNA cancer vaccines (Phase 3, -44% recurrence) and MCED-driven stage shift. Proxy: US all-cancer survival (5-yr 69%) is the frontier proxy for 'all solid tumour cases' because it is the best-measured, most favourable population; it includes haematological cancers, and a global reading is much later.
blockers: Technical: metastatic disease remains largely incurable (stage IV 5-yr survival 8-31%; pancreatic 8% overall)
Structural floor: 10-yr survival is observable only ~5-9 yr after diagnosis
Funding/policy: FY2026 request proposes a 37.3% NCI cut; FDA staff attrition >18% (legacy)
Evidential: no all-site 10-yr survival series in the ledger (gather request)
basis.benchmark: 80% of solid tumour cases reach 10-year survival
basis.change_note: Rubric correction v2, no new evidence; status stays red. The previous assessment (2026-09-30-milestone-taming-cancer, v1) gave its ETA as '>10 years', a status band, and declined to forecast for lack of a survival series. RUBRIC.md v2 §4.1 forbids both. It did not convert the level to the milestone's 10-yr quantity or use the long-run survival trend as a reference class, and it ignored the 10-yr follow-up floor. Modelled as exponential hazard reduction, the median is 2063 (p10 2042, p90 open).

label: Distant: ~20% of NCDs caught pre-symptomatic (est.) vs >50%; no MCED approved yet; ETA ~2044
rationale: No ledger record measures the pre-symptomatic share for any of the four disease classes. Background estimates for high-income countries average ~20% across classes (cancer ~15%, CVD ~10%, type 2 diabetes ~55%, neurodegeneration ~2%) against >50%. The drivers are real but pre-population-scale: MCED (PATHFINDER 2 detected >7x more cancers, 53.5% early stage) has no approval, and the cleared Alzheimer's blood tests are for symptomatic patients. Logistic adoption curves after approval and coverage floors, checked against the mammography and CRC screening ramps, put the median at ~2044 (80% range 2037-2060), so red (Distant).

basis.rule: Milestone red: median ETA 2044 > made_at + 10 yr (RUBRIC.md §4: Distant); the projection (NHS-Galleri results) and announcements do not lift the status

eta.method: S-curve (logistic adoption per disease class after a regulatory/coverage floor), Monte Carlo; cross-checked against screening-adoption reference classes, discounted proponent dates and the prev ETA
eta.calc: Gap (background HIC estimates, not in ledger): cancer ~15%, CVD ~10%, metabolic/T2D ~55%, neuro ~2% -> equal class-weighted ~20% vs >50% = 2.4x. Logistic (ceiling, midpoint, scale): cancer (70%, 2040, 4.5 yr; MCED approval ~2027-28, coverage ~2030), CVD (60%, 2042, 5; AI-ECG/CAC/opportunistic CT AI; 873 FDA AI radiology devices, +115 in 2025), metabolic (85%, 2035, 5), neuro (60%, 2042, 4.5; needs preventive AD therapy). Central path: 2030 24%, 2035 31%, 2040 43%, 2043 50.1%. MC (N=200k; common midpoint shift N(0, 6 yr), per-class N(0, 4 yr), ceilings +/-10 pts): p10 2037, p50 2044, p90 2052; p90 widened to 2060 for the stricter 'each class >50%' reading (~2049 central) and non-HIC populations. P(by Oct 2036) 0.09. Reference class (background): US mammography ~29% -> ~70% in ~13 yr after 1987; CRC screening ~35% -> ~70% in ~20 yr; lung LDCT ~16-18% after 9 yr. MCED approval ~2028 + 13-20 yr -> 2041-48. Proponent GRAIL PMA 'H1 2026' (pre-rubric, projection) x1.5-3 -> approval 2027-29. Prev v1 ETA '>10 years (not estimable)'.
eta.cruxes: Earlier: NHS-Galleri shows stage shift/mortality benefit; FDA approves an MCED test with Medicare coverage; a preventive anti-amyloid trial (AHEAD 3-45/TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 3) succeeds, making preclinical AD screening actionable; opportunistic imaging/ECG AI is deployed at scale. Later: NHS-Galleri null; MCED PMA delayed or rejected; reimbursement blocked. Gather: measured screen-detected/pre-symptomatic share per class (Routes to Diagnosis, undiagnosed-diabetes share).

basis.path: Cancer: MCED blood tests (Galleri PATHFINDER 2: >7x detection added to USPSTF screening, 53.5% early stage, 99.5% specificity; Cancerguard launched; NHS-Galleri 140k RCT pending) plus AI risk prediction (Clairity De Novo). Neuro: FDA-cleared pTau blood tests (symptomatic use) and the AA blood-biomarker guideline. CVD: AI-enabled imaging/ECG (873 FDA AI radiology devices). Metabolic: routine HbA1c testing. The proxy is background per-class detection-route estimates, because the ledger has no measurement; that uncertainty widens the range.
blockers: Regulatory: no MCED test approved; no mortality-benefit RCT result yet
Clinical: pre-symptomatic AD detection lacks an approved preventive therapy; cleared tests are for symptomatic patients
Evidential: no ledger measurement of the pre-symptomatic share for any class (gather request)
basis.benchmark: >50% of major NCD cases (cancer, cardiovascular, metabolic, neurodegeneration) caught pre-symptomatic
basis.change_note: Rubric correction v2, no new evidence; status stays red. The previous assessment (2026-09-30-milestone-precise-screening, v1) gave the ETA as '>10 years (not estimable: no series)'. RUBRIC.md v2 §4.1 forbids both the band and the refusal: it requires tying the milestone to drivers or a reference class. It also ignored the metabolic and cardiovascular classes instead of estimating them. Modelling per-class S-curve adoption gives a median of 2044 (p10 2037, p90 2060).

label: Distant: 80+ dementia ~17-27% vs <5%; incidence -0.7-1.1%/yr, faster with prevention; ETA ~2092
rationale: Dementia prevalence after 80 is about 22% (US ADAMS 24% at 80-89 and 37% at 90+; NHS 1 in 6 over-80s for Alzheimer's alone) against <5%, a 4.4x gap. Age-standardised incidence has fallen ~20% over 2-3 decades (0.7-1.1%/yr), which alone takes ~165 years. Allowing prevention (intensive BP control RR 0.85, anti-amyloid/tau drugs) to lift the rate to a median 2.5%/yr from the early 2030s, plus a ~6-year prevalence lag, puts the median at ~2092 (80% range 2060 to after 2100), so red (Distant).

basis.rule: Milestone red: median ETA 2092 > made_at + 10 yr (RUBRIC.md §4: Distant)

eta.method: trend (exponential decline of age-specific prevalence) with a regime change for preventive therapies, plus a prevalence-stock lag, Monte Carlo; cross-checked against a reference class (Framingham decline) and the prev ETA
eta.calc: Gap: 80+ prevalence ~22% (18-27%; ADAMS 24% at 80-89/37% at 90+, NHS AD-only 1 in 6) vs 5% = 4.4x, ln 1.48 (2.1 halvings). Trend: Lancet -20% over 2-3 decades = ln(1/0.8)/30..20 = 0.74-1.12%/yr; trend only ln(4.4)/0.009 = 165 yr (~2180). Two regimes: r0 until T_s ~ U(2030, 2036), then r1 ~ lognormal(median 2.5%/yr, p10 1.0%, p90 6.2%); prevalence lag U(4, 8) yr. Central: 2016-2033 at 0.9% removes 0.153; (1.48-0.153)/0.025 = 53 yr -> 2086 + 6 lag = 2092. MC (N=200k): p10 2060.2, p50 2092.4, P(by 2100) 0.57 -> p90 null. P(by Oct 2036) ~0. Reference (background): Framingham ~20%/decade = 2.2%/yr -> ln(4.4)/0.022 = 67 yr -> ~2085-90. Prev v1 ETA '>100 years (110-210)'.
eta.cruxes: Earlier: a preventive anti-amyloid trial (AHEAD 3-45/TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 3) shows a large incidence cut; anti-tau (etalanetug) clinical benefit; cohort data showing >=2%/yr incidence decline; the best-placed country (SHARE low end) counting. Later: prevention trials fail; obesity/diabetes reverse the incidence decline; treatment lengthens survival with dementia, raising prevalence. Gather: an 80+ prevalence series (HRS-HCAP, CFAS, SHARE waves).

basis.path: Risk-factor reduction (cardiovascular health, education; intensive BP control RR 0.85 over 4 yr in 33,995 adults) plus disease-modifying drugs (donanemab -27% progression at 3 yr; lecanemab modelled 3.5-8.3 yr delay; etalanetug -90% plasma tau, Fast Track). Reaching 5% needs a ~77% cut in age-specific prevalence across AD, vascular and Lewy-body dementia.
blockers: Technical: approved therapies slow but do not prevent or stop decline; 2025 Phase 3 failures (oral semaglutide, posdinemab); ARIA safety monitoring
Structural: prevalence in 80+ lags incidence by years; preventive trials take 4+ years
Evidential: no 80+ prevalence time series in the ledger (gather request)
basis.change_note: Rubric correction v2, no new evidence; status stays red. The previous assessment (2026-09-30-milestone-unbroken-mind, v1) extrapolated only the historical incidence trend in a straight line and reported '>100 years (110-210)', a pessimistic bound with no median or 80% range. It ignored the acceleration paths (BP control, anti-amyloid/tau prevention) and the prevalence lag that RUBRIC.md v2 §4.1 asks to model. With them, the median is 2092 (p10 2060, p90 open): still red, but ~90 years earlier than the trend-only figure.

label: Distant: best human clock reversal 2.6-3.2 yrs, flat since 2019, vs >=10 + less disease; ETA ~2043
rationale: The best human biological-age reversals are 2.5 years (TRIIM 2019), 3.23 (Fitzgerald 2021) and 2.6 (Buck TPE+IVIG 2025), flat for six years against the 10-year target, and no trial shows reduced disease incidence. The ETA rests instead on the partial-reprogramming driver: 7.42 years in vitro (SB000 preprint), AI-redesigned factors, and first human trials announced or just dosed. Modelled as a chain, a systemic human ≥10-year reversal (median ~2033) is followed by a ≥5-year outcome trial and validation (~7.5 years), giving a median of ~2043 (80% range 2036 to never). That is more than 10 years out, so red (Distant).

basis.rule: Milestone red: median ETA 2043 > made_at + 10 yr (RUBRIC.md §4: Distant); the milestone quantity itself is flat 2019-2025, so the ETA is tied to the reprogramming driver

eta.method: structural-floor chain (human >=10-yr systemic reversal, then outcome trial plus validation) driven by the partial-reprogramming pipeline, Monte Carlo; cross-checked against reference classes (CAR-T, gene therapy, statins), discounted proponent dates and the prev ETA
eta.calc: Gap: best human reversal 2.6-3.23 yr (2019-2025, flat) vs >=10 yr = 3.1-3.8x on clocks; the functional and disease-incidence components are at zero. Driver: SB000 7.42 yr in vitro (2025); GPT-4b micro factors >50x marker expression; ER-100 first-in-human Q1 2026 (announcement, local eye); RTR242 dosed Dec 2025. Stage A (systemic human >=10-yr clock+function reversal) = 2026 + lognormal(median 7, p10 3 yr) -> p10 2029, p50 2033, p90 2042. Stage B (start ~1.5 + >=5-yr outcome trial, cf. SELECT ~5 yr / TAME ~6 yr, + ~1 yr readout/replication) = lognormal(median 7.5, p10 5.5 yr). P(modality fails, no alternative by 2100) 0.20 (cf. UNITY senolytics). MC (N=200k): p10 2036.5, p50 2042.7, P(by 2100) 0.80 -> p90 null. P(by Oct 2036) 0.12. Reference: CAR-T first-in-human -> approval 7 yr (2010-17); gene therapy 22-27 yr; statins approval -> 4S outcome trial 7 yr; 2026 + ~16 yr -> ~2042. Proponent 'this decade' x1.5-3 -> A ~2032-38, +7.5 -> 2040-45. Gene-therapy capacity: 36 approved, 679 clinical-stage (knowledge-beyond 2025-08-01-asgct-pipeline-q2-rv). AI driver ~6-month METR doubling (robots-software metr-50-horizon-by-release) speeds factor design, not trials. Prev v1 ETA '>10 years'.
eta.cruxes: Earlier: ER-100 safety/efficacy data 2026-27 and a systemic reprogramming IND; any human trial with >=5-yr reversal across multiple clocks plus function; a TAME-like geroprotector outcome result. Later: teratoma or other reprogramming safety signals; ER-100 delays; regulators refuse aging/multimorbidity as an indication; more senolytic-style failures. Gather: human clock-reversal results from 2026 trials; outcome-trial status (TAME, PEARL).

basis.path: Partial epigenetic reprogramming (SB000, GPT-4b micro-designed factors, Life Bio ER-100 first-in-human, NewLimit, Retro ~$1B), plasma exchange (Buck TPE+IVIG 2.6 yr), GLP-1 organ-clock effects and geroprotectors validated in mice (rapamycin+trametinib +34.9%, ITP rapamycin+acarbose +36.6%). None has a human outcome trial.
blockers: Technical: no human intervention exceeds ~3.2 yr of clock reversal; systemic reprogramming not yet in humans (safety: loss of cell identity/teratoma)
Structural: 'validated ... with reductions in disease incidence' needs a multi-year outcome trial and replication
Regulatory: aging is not an approved indication, which complicates outcome-trial design
basis.benchmark: >=10 years of biological-age reversal (epigenetic clocks + functional biomarkers) with reduced age-related disease incidence
basis.change_note: Rubric correction v2, no new evidence; status stays red. The previous assessment (2026-09-30-milestone-the-long-middle-age, v1) answered '>10 years', a status band, and took the flat human clock-reversal record as the whole answer. RUBRIC.md v2 §4.1 requires tying a stalled quantity to its driver (here the reprogramming pipeline) and modelling the structural floors (outcome trial, validation) with cross-checks. Doing so gives a median of 2043 (p10 2036, p90 open). Its verdict 'Stalled' is replaced by 'Distant' because the median lies beyond 10 years.
